title: Uniform dimension bound for fibres of a finite-type morphism
statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and assume $Y$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. There exists an integer $d\geq0$ such that for every point $y\in Y$ the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_y$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $d$. Empty fibres are allowed and have dimension $-\infty$.

proof.text: Since f is quasi-compact and Y is quasi-compact, X is quasi-compact. Lean uses QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace f, the whole-space case of the quasi-compact preimage theorem.

source.place: Tag 0A3V, lemma-morphism-finite-type-bounded-dimension; Tag 02FZ for the local openness step

proof.text: For each x in X, the whole scheme-theoretic fibre over f(x) is quasi-compact and locally of finite type over its residue field, by base change. Apply the existing finite-type dimension theorem exists_topologicalKrullDim_le to its structure morphism. The local dimension e(x) is bounded by the dimension of this fibre. It is nonnegative because every open neighbourhood contains the point and its irreducible closed singleton closure. Eliminating bottom and top in WithBot ENat therefore gives a natural number equal to e(x). This uses the quasi-compactness of f already assumed in the statement and avoids constructing a separate affine fibre chart for finiteness.

source.place: Tag 0A3V, lemma-morphism-finite-type-bounded-dimension; Tag 02FZ for the local openness step

proof.text: Choose affine opens U about x and V about f(x) with U contained in the inverse image of V, and let g : U to V be f.resLE. An open immersion of sources induces an open immersion of fibres by pullback.map. An open immersion of targets is injective, so composing with it leaves the set-theoretic fibres identical. The fibre homeomorphisms, homeomorphism invariance of local dimension, and the open-subspace equality identify the local dimensions of g and f at corresponding points. The affine coordinate comparison identifies the former with the local dimension in the ring fibre of the finite-type map on global sections. Apply fibre_dimension_bounded_open_upstairs at the prime corresponding to x, with its natural dimension e(x). Pull its open neighbourhood back by isoSpec and push it forward by U inclusion. This gives an open W(x) about x where every local fibre dimension is bounded by e(x).

source.place: Tag 0A3V, lemma-morphism-finite-type-bounded-dimension; Tag 02FZ for the local openness step

proof.text: The open neighbourhoods W(x) cover X, so quasi-compactness gives a finite subcover. Let d be the Finset.sup of its natural bounds, with bottom zero in the empty case. Each point of each fibre corresponds, via fiberHomeo and fiberι, to a point x of X, and its local dimension is therefore at most d. The equality of global dimension with the supremum of local dimensions bounds the whole fibre by d. Empty fibres are included because their supremum is bottom; if X is empty the finite supremum gives d = 0.
